case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 20-5-2008 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 6262 of 2005, 6671 of 2004, 2678 of 2005, 1512 and 1513 of 2006 and 3797 of 2003).
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J: These leave petitions filed under Article 103 of the Constitution arise out of a common judgment and order dated 20-5-2008 passed in Writ Petition No. 6262 of 2005 heard and disposed of along with Writ Petition Nos. 2678 of 2005, 3797 of 2003, 6671 of 2004, 1512 and 1513 of 2006, making the Rules absolute. 
2. The facts and circumstances giving rise to the filing of the writ petitions are similar and the contesting respondents, the grounds as well as the issue involved in the writ petitions are same. Accordingly, the Rules issued in the writ petitions were heard and disposed of by a common judgment. The petitioners in the writ petitions are however, different. The common case in the writ petitions is that the respective case lands originally belonged to Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and the petitioners are the successors-in-interest of the tenants under the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and accordingly, in the CS Khatian the respective case lands stand in the name of Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and thereafter after the acquisition of the land of the Zaminders on cessation of the Seminary system the rent receiving interest of the Mouza under which the case lands belonged was acquired by the Government under section 3(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 vide notification No.2773 LR dated 26-2-1952 and the said notification of acquisition was published in the Dhaka Gazette on 24-3-1952, whereby it was notified that all interest of rent receiving vested in the Government with effect from 14-4-1952 and the schedule given in the said Gazette notification includes the Mouza under which the case lands are situated and that thereafter by a notification No.3126 LR dated 27-2-1956 published in the Dhaka Gazette on 29-2-1956; the Government acquired the lands of the Bhawal Raj Courts of Wards Estate, in respect of which the rent receiving interest was acquired earlier, on declaration of the compensation assessment rolls under section 43(2) read with sections 46C and 46E(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and thereby the respective case lands of the writ petitioners vested in the Government with effect from the date of publication of the said notifications and thus, since then the tenants under the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate became tenants under the Government in respect of such vested lands. Accordingly, during SA Survey Operation the names of the writ petitioners and or their-predecessors-in-interest were correctly recorded in the SA Khatian without any objection from any quarter and thereafter during the Revisional Survey Operation, the names of the writ petitioners and or their predecessors-in-interest were duly recorded in the RS Khatian correctly and without objection. Thus the petitioners directly or through their predecessors-in-interest have been owning and possessing their respective case land as tenants on payment of rates and rents initially to the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and subsequently, after cessation of Zamindary system, to the Revenue Authority of the Government openly and publicly without any objection. During the recent Mahanagor Survey Operation the Revenue Authority found the writ-petitioners in possession of their respective case lands and accordingly, the draft records of right was prepared in their respective names in accordance with law i.e. under Rule 29 of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955, (hereinafter referred to as the said Rules, 1955). The leave petitioner Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate filed objection under Rule 30 of the said Rules for removing the names of the writ petitioners as appearing against their respective possession in their respective case lands in the draft records of right challenging their tenancy and that the revenue authority after full-fledged hearing rejected the objection of the leave petitioner and being aggrieved there against the leave petitioner preferred appeals under Rule 31 of said Rules, 1955 unsuccessfully and thereby draft record of right was published in respective names of the writ petitioners under Rule 33 of the said Rules, 1955 but it appears that the leave petitioner Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate filed an application mentioning Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules for correction of the published draft record of right and on the basis of said application fresh hearing was taken and the names of the writ petitioners were substituted by the name Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate as tenants in respect of the case lands in the respective Khatians on the basis of the CS Khatian, disbelieving the intermediary transfers made during the period till the promulgation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and disregarding the acquisition of the rent receiving interest and vesting of the case lands in the Government through gazette notifications dated 26-2-1952 and 27-2-1976 referred to above, and the fact of payment of Rates and Taxes to the Government by the writ petitioners in respect of their respective case lands as tenants and that though the names of the writ petitioners were ordered to be substituted by the name of the leave petitioner but the writ petitioners were ordered to be shown as "illegal possessors though force" and thus the possession of the writ petitioners in the case lands is admitted. Being aggrieved as such the writ petitioners moved the High Court Division and obtained the Rules and the High Court Division after hearing the parties made the Rules absolute observing, amongst others: 
"We requested Mr. Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed to assist us in finding where said respondent No.2 stands in the scheme of the Act. He was very responsive and submitted a written submission. 
He submitted that by the Bangladesh Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976 (Ordinance No. IX of 1976) under new section 2A the power of the Court of Wards vested in the Divisional Commissioner of respective areas. By the Bangladesh Laws Board of Land Administration in place of the Government is the Court of Wards, which reverted to pre-President's Order 12 of 1973. 
He submitted that after acquisition of rent receiving interest of the concerned estates, the tenants of the Bhawal Raj Estate were no more tenants under them and they became "Malik" directly under the Government. Article 143(c) of the Constitution is not applicable in the case of present record of rights and the circular dated 10-11-2002 is illegal and any action taken thereupon must be set aside. 
Lastly, he submitted that management of the properties of disqualified owners by the Court of Wards is a matter of long past. Either they have overcome their disqualification in the meantime or have died leaving heirs to inherit the estates. A relevant question therefore, arises if there is at all any necessity or scope for such Court of Wards to function in Bangladesh. That is a matter which is best to be left to be considered and decided by the legislature. But the country has suffered the "Enemy Property" and "abandoned property" and the litigations enough to take lesson. He however, cautioned against any strong observation from this Division in respect of the two Courts of Wards, which are still functioning in the country and the, attention of proper quarters might be drawn. 
But one cannot prevent the law to take its own course. After the publication of general notification No. 2773 dated 26-2-52 under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the notification No. 3126 dated 27-2-56 declaring the Compensation Assessment-rolls under section 43(2) read with section 46 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, all rent receiving interests stood acquired and the tenants of any such rent receivers became "Malik" directly under the Government and all non-retainable khas land vested in the Government". 
In the case of Bangladesh vs. Madan Gopal Jew 33 DLR (AD) 13, the Appellate Division set at rest all controversy regarding the impact of such wholesale acquisition as under: 
"it is to be further observed that it is now well settled on the authority of Jalil Ahmed vs. Province of East Pakistan 19 DLR 106 decided by a Special Bench and affirmed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Tanvir Ahmed Siddiky vs. Province of East Pakistan 20 DLR (SC) 144 = PLD 1968 SC 185 that on the publication of the notification under section 3 of the Act, all rent receiving interests including that of Debater and Waqf Estate stood acquired and all non-retainable khas land also stood vested in the Government." 
3. Section 8A of the Court of Wards Act, 1879 provides that if the rent-receiving interests of a ward in any estate under the charge of the Court are acquired under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, then notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, the remaining properties of such ward including khas lands under the charge of the Court shall continue to remain under its charge and shall be managed in accordance with the provision of this Act, as if such Ward was a disqualified proprietor of an estate. Section A was inserted by section 2 of the East Bengal Court of Wards (Amendment) Act, 1952 (Act X of 1952). Then, under section 2A of the Bangladesh Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976 (Ordinance IX of 1976) the Commissioners shall, until otherwise specifically provided for by law, possess and exercise within the powers and authority now vested in the Courts of Wards, subject to the control and direction of the Government and to such restrictions and provisions as the Government may prescribe, and that, on the technical ground on maintainability of the writ petition, when confronted, Mr. TH Khan failed to produce any gazette notification of final publication of the recent record of rights. He said due to the pendency of the Rules, the record of rights could not be finally published. Under section 145A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, when the Government would establish the Land Survey Tribunal only after final publication of last revised record of rights prepared under section 144 and after establishment of such Tribunals, any suit challenging correctness of the last revised record of rights shall lie in such Tribunal. 
Mr. Nurul Amin and Abul Quashem adopted the arguments of Mr. TH Khan, Mr. Qashem however, insisted for decision on title. We can only say if any person on behalf of so-called Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate or Bhawal Raj Estate is still aggrieved he can go to a Civil Court of competent jurisdiction for vindication. He does not have any remedy under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. They have already exercised their choice by institution of Title Suit No. 188 of 2006 in the 4th Court of Joint District Judge at Dhaka for declaration of title in certain lands and they may pursue the cause there. 
4. We have perused the leave petitions impugned judgment and order, the writ petitions, affidavit-in-opposition and the annexures thereto. We have considered the submissions made by the learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner and also the learned Advocates of the respondents, who filed caveat. The learned Additional Attorney-General appeared for the Government. The learned Advocate for the leave petitioner submitted that admittedly the case land belonged to Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and that while passing impugned order allowing the application filed under Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 in disposing of the appeals, the appellate officer disbelieved the transfers of the case lands made as claimed by the respective writ petitioners; and ordered for substitution of the name of the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate in place of the names of the respective writ petitioners appearing against the respective case lands in the draft record of rights, but possession of the writ petitioners have been maintained. The learned' Advocate for the leave petitioner submitted that the alleged transfer of the case lands in the names of "the writ petitioners and or their predecessors-in-interest" have been shown fraudulently on the basis of forged documents and that in the meantime the record of right in respect of the case lands on the basis of Mohanagar Survey have been published in accordance with law in the name of the leave petitioner Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and therefore the writ petitioners cannot get any relief in the present forum and they are to move the Civil Court for relief, if any. The learned Additional Attorney-General while making his submission in favour of the leave petitioner found it difficult to support the leave petitioner, since confronted with the gazette notifications dated 25-3-1952 showing acquisition of rent receiving interest under section 3(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in respect of the lands covered by Mouza 262 under JL No.2 and the gazetee notification dated 29-2-1956 showing acquisition and vesting of the lands, in respect of which the rent receiving interest have been acquired, under section 43(2), 46C and 46E(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 in favour of the government and the ground rent payment receipts given by the revenue office in favour of the writ petitioners in respect of the case lands admitting their tenancy under the Government, copy of which has been annexed by the writ-petitioner of WP No. 1449 of 2008. 
5. The learned Advocate appearing for the aviators i.e. writ-petitioners, submitted that the leave petitioner Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate has challenged their ownership i.e. tenancy under the Government, malafide and for illegal gains. It has been submitted that the application filed under Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules is a misconceived application and not entertain able, inasmuch as the said application did not contain any ingredient of any fraud and that it is the established principle of law that a mere allegation of fraud is not sufficient and unless the ingredients of fraud is disclosed in the petition, no cognizance thereof is to be taken. The aviators produced copy of the application of the leave petitioner filed allegedly under Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules, which runs as under:

6. The learned Advocate placed before us the Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules, 1555, which runs as under: 
"42A. Correction of fraudulent entry before final publication of record-of-rights.—The Revenue-officer, with the additional designation of Settlement Officer shall, on receipt of an application or on receipt of an official report for the correction of an entry that has been procured by fraud in record-of-rights before final publication thereof, after consulting relevant records and making such other enquiries as he deems necessary, direct excision of the fraudulent entry and his act in doing so shall not be open to appeal. At the same time, the Revenue-officer shall make the correct entry after giving the parties concerned a hearing and recording his finding in a formal proceeding for the purpose of future reference." 
and submitted that there being no correction made in the records of right in the recent khatian prepared during Mahanagar Survey and the names of the tenants and their respective possession in respect of the case lands as appearing being in accordance with records made during previous Survey Operations i.e. in the SA Khatian and RS Khatian, the question of commission of any fraud does not arise and therefore Rule 42A under reference cannot have any application in the instant case. Further, there being no mention of any act of fraud in the body of the application of the leave petitioner dated 14-7-2002, as filed, the application as framed and filed was liable to be rejected in limini and the entertainment of the application, as filed, mentioning Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955, was illegal and without lawful authority and the impugned order passed on the basis of such illegal application cannot have any legal effect and liable to be set aside. 
7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions of the learned Advocates of the respective parties and on perusal of the Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 as well as the application filed by the leave petitioner Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate dated 14-7-2002, quoted above, and the gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956 as well as ground rent payment receipts issued by the Government revenue office and earlier by the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and also the transfer made through registered deed of gift and having regard to the fact that the SA record of right and RS record of right were correctly prepared in the names of the writ petitioners and or their predecessors-in-interest in respect of their respective lands and also the fact of admission, as to the possession of the writ petitioners in their respective case lands in the draft Mahanagar record of right, we do not find any reason to interfere with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division. The learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner, when confronted with the aforesaid gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956, as to acquisition of rent receiving interest and the vesting of lands of the leave petitioners, including the case lands, found it difficult to substantiate the locus standi of the leave petitioner in challenging the draft records of right prepared in the names of the respective writ petitioners in respect of their respective case lands prepared during the Mohanagar Survey. Further, with the publication of the gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956 the leave petitioner ceased to have any right, title and interest and possession in the case lands, because of acquisition, and vesting of said lands in the Government. The learned Additional Attorney- General could not deny the granting of the ground rent payment receipts, copy of which have been annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition, admitting the writ petitioners as tenants under the Government. 
8. On plain reading of the Rule 42A, quoted above, it appears that Settlement Officer is empowered to pass order only on receipt of an application or on receipt of an official report, for correction of an entry in the record of right, procured by fraud, before final publication thereof. Thus the said Rule cannot be applicable in the instant case, inasmuch as the record of right as prepared is in accordance with the past records of right prepared during SA Operation and RS Operation and there being no change as to the names as appearing in the said records of right the question of fraud in recording the entry of names in the recent record of right prepared after the Mahanagar Survey does not arise. Apart from that after final publication of the record of right, after the SA Survey the only mode for correction of the same was through Civil Court and thus subsequent to preparation of SA record of right, the RS record of right was prepared and after final publication thereof the mode for correction of any wrong entry appearing in the RS record was through Civil Court and without moving the Civil Court no correction in recent records of right is lawful or permissible and as such the draft record of right in the instant case having been prepared following the preparation of the SA and RS records in accordance with law, the attempts of the leave petitioner for correction under Rules 30 and 31 of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 have failed. The plain reading of the application dated 14-7-2002, quoted above, allegedly filed under Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955, ex-facie appears to be a vague application, inasmuch as the said appellation contains no specific allegation of any act of fraud and it is the settled principle of law that an application, not having disclosed any act of fraud in its body, is not entertain able and liable to be rejected. Without correcting the SA Khatian and RS Khatian as prepared in respect of the case lands in accordance with law earlier, the leave petitioner cannot get its name entered in the recent record of right prepared during Mohanagar Survey allegedly only on the basis of CS Khatian. 
9. Thus we are of the view that the leave petitioner had no locus standi to challenge the draft Mahanagar Survey Khatian as prepared in the names of the respective writ petitioners, at least after publication of the gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956. 
10. It has been submitted that in the body of the impugned judgment the High Court Division made certain observations as to the locus standi of the Manager of the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate in representing the Estate and the very existence of Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate itself in the eye of law, and hence the learned Advocate for the leave petitioner submitted that the such observations as appearing in the body of the impugned judgment need be corrected by expunging the same. On perusal of the Court of Wards Act, 1879, it appears that the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate was created under the said Act and the Management and Guardianship of said Wards is to be managed by the manager appointed under section 20 of the said Act and section 39 of the Court of Wards Act, 1879 provides that every manager appointed by the Court shall have power to manage all property which may be committed to his charge, to collect the rents of the land entrusted to him, as well as all other money due to the ward, and to grant receipts, therefore; and may, under the orders of the Court, grant or reduce such leases and farm as may be necessary for the good management of the property. The "Manager' under the said Act is also responsible to look after the interest of wards as if the property is his own and is also a counter. The manager of Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate, appointed under section 20 of the Court of Wards Act, is to look after the retained properties till those are released in accordance with the provision of the Court of Wards Act. The Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate shall remain in existence and is to be managed by such manager until released in accordance with the Act. The Estate of the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate is being managed under the Court of Wards Act and directly managed and looked after by the manager appointed and the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate, at present, is functioning in accordance with law. Thus the observations made regarding existence of the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and as to its functioning and locus standi, in the body of impugned judgment passed by the High Court Division are expunged and will be of no effect in the eye of law. 
Accordingly, with the above observations the leave petitions are dismissed. 
End.
